status_summary: No FTC task force on ESG or DEI collusion was found, and a Federal Register search for FTC documents mentioning ESG since 2025-01-20 returned none. The FTC has pursued related theories through individual cases. It joined DOJ in a 2025-05-22 statement of interest backing state attorneys general who allege that asset managers used coal holdings to restrain output (Texas v. BlackRock). It obtained consent orders barring advertising agencies from coordinating ad placement on publishers' political or ideological viewpoints: Omnicom and Interpublic (proposed 2025-06-23, finalized in September 2025, with terms that also cover DEI-commitment criteria), then WPP, Publicis and Dentsu (2026-04-15, with eight states) and Havas (reported 2026-07-05). A separate FTC probe of Media Matters over the same boycott allegations was blocked by a preliminary injunction; after argument on 2026-04-13 the FTC withdrew its investigative demand and the D.C. Circuit dismissed the appeal on 2026-05-04. The actions differ from the chapter in design: no task force, no private equity focus, and they rest on Sherman Act and unfair-methods-of-competition theories.

timeline.event: DOJ's Antitrust Division, joined by the FTC, files a statement of interest in Texas v. BlackRock (E.D. Tex.) supporting state attorneys general who allege that BlackRock, State Street and Vanguard used holdings in competing coal producers to induce lower output, and urging denial of the asset managers' motion to dismiss.

FTC announces a proposed consent order in Omnicom's 13.5 billion dollar acquisition of Interpublic that bars coordinating or steering ad spending away from publishers based on political or ideological viewpoints (vote 2-0-1, Commissioner Meador recused); the Federal Register notice follows on 2025-06-26.

FTC approves the final Omnicom and Interpublic order, which trade press reports broadened the restrictions to cover third-party journalistic-standards ratings and DEI commitments as ad-buying criteria (date from the article's publication, which refers to the previous Friday).

D.C. Circuit, 2-1, declines to lift an August 2025 preliminary injunction that bars the FTC from pursuing its civil investigative demand to Media Matters in the advertising-boycott probe; the district court had found the probe likely retaliatory in violation of the First Amendment, and the panel did not rule on the merits.

Thirteen state attorneys general announce a 29.5 million dollar settlement with Vanguard in the same ESG antitrust suit; claims against BlackRock and State Street continue. The sources do not show the FTC or DOJ as parties to the settlement.

At D.C. Circuit argument in the Media Matters appeal, an FTC lawyer says the agency is negotiating settlements with other targets of its probe into whether advertising and media groups colluded to boycott online platforms.

FTC, with eight states, files a complaint in the Northern District of Texas against WPP, Publicis and Dentsu alleging collusion through trade-group brand-safety standards, with stipulated final orders entered the same day (no admission of liability; barred criteria include political or ideological viewpoints and DEI commitments; ten-year term with five-year monitor).
After oral argument, the FTC withdraws its civil investigative demand to Media Matters and the D.C. Circuit dismisses the FTC appeal.

A local news report dated this day says Havas Media Group USA, described as the last of six large agencies to be covered, consented to a similar order approved by the Northern District of Texas (Commission vote 1-0-1); date is the report date and the filing date is not given.

title: Create an FTC task force on ESG and DEI collusion and unfair trade practices
uncertainties: Whether the FTC has an internal ESG or DEI working group that was never announced cannot be ruled out; only the Federal Register (zero FTC documents mentioning ESG) and press coverage were checked. The 2026 WPP, Publicis, Dentsu and Havas events rest on a law-firm alert, trade press and a single local-news report; the FTC's own April 2026 press release URL returned a 404 when fetched, so no FTC page confirms them. The September 2025 final order date is inferred from an article date. The outcome of the Media Matters appeal and of the BlackRock motion to dismiss were not found. Private equity enforcement relating to ESG was not found, though FTC private equity cases on other theories exist and were not assessed. Whether these ad-agency actions count as 'ESG/DEI collusion' is a classification judgment: the FTC frames them as viewpoint-based boycotts.
